candidateIdentity.variantName: Horizon on integrated Druber strap; titanium bracelet included

sourceChecks.note: BOLDR's country-contextualized exact product route and embedded Storefront payload identify Odyssey Horizon SKU ODY-TI-40-H-BL as available with inventory, USD 799, and Add to cart. The page publishes the 40 mm Titanium+ case, 13 mm complete thickness including glass, 48 mm lug-to-lug, 20 mm nominal lug size, 91 g full weight on the integrated Druber strap, 125 g on the separately supplied integrated titanium bracelet, Miyota 9075, 42-hour reserve, 300 m resistance, screw-down crown, sapphire, Swiss Super-LumiNova application, and both attachment configurations. Retrieved 2026-08-30.

BOLDR's December 2024 launch release identifies Horizon as one of the reimagined Odyssey Titanium colors, specifies Miyota 9075 GMT with an independently adjustable local hour, and explicitly documents the 4 o'clock date window. This resolves date presence from primary family-launch evidence tied to Horizon rather than from an assumed movement function or product photograph. Retrieved 2026-08-30.

Miyota's current caliber 9075 technical page publishes -10/+30 seconds per day, approximately 42 hours of running time, 28,800 vibrations per hour, automatic and hand winding, stop seconds, central GMT, and independent local-hour adjustment. BOLDR explicitly identifies 9075 in the exact watch, so the caliber contract is exact-applicable. Retrieved 2026-08-30.

The exact Horizon dealer page corroborates the configuration and displays a lume photograph, but its categorical 'strong lume' prose describes the Odyssey platform generally. It provides no charge protocol, elapsed observation, timed decay, or independent exact-Horizon comparison, so it cannot establish weak, moderate, or strong performance. Retrieved 2026-08-30 after the narrow Perplexity pass.

The exact Horizon retailer route corroborates the physical watch but states only Swiss Super-LumiNova material. It supplies no performance method or result and therefore cannot close the lume-grade gate. Retrieved 2026-08-30.

Worn & Wound's exact hands-on review identifies the sky-blue Horizon variant, documents the luminous hands and indices, and records that after normal overnight wear the lume was still glowing until morning. This is a direct elapsed overnight observation on the exact reference, supporting strong performance; the material-only sources remain insufficient on their own. Retrieved 2026-08-31.
